rules.statement: A procedure adopted by a party must be communicated to the parties involved, and failure to do so may result in a denial of natural justice if it prejudices any party.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The Bank is not compelled to adopt a particular procedure but what procedure it adopts must be made known to the parties. If any party is prejudiced for want of such knowledge it may result in a denial of natural justice depending on the extent of the prejudice caused. (2) The notices of the inquiry give the impression that the scheduled inquiry is a formal inquiry. When on 15.12.77 the inquiry was postponed to 14.12.77 the petitioner-respondent (M) was entitled to expect the formal inquiry to continue. (3) The failure to issue a copy of the objection's which the inquiring officer himself had ordered to be copied to the lawyer of the other party discloses a lack of the judicial spirit required of an inquirer. (4) While seeking the submissions of S's lawyer the Bank's only contact with M was for the purpose of persuading her to amicably settle the dispute. (5) the duty of making the correct decision was exclusively on the Bank and there was no burden on the lawyer of the owner to activate the Bank. (6) Whether or not the failure to permit oral hearings would constitute a denial of natural justice will depend on the facts and circumstances and the issue in each case
